groups.text: It is currently 23 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Developers are expanding the capabilities of local AI through a new release from llama.cpp. The update adds speculative decoding support for GLM-5.2, specifically integrating NextN and MTP targets. This allows the software to use a draft head that runs dense MLA while keeping the main context filtered to trunk layers. To facilitate this, the team added a graph builder and nextn tensor loading via a presence probe. Users can now choose between different export options for GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM. Selecting the no-mtp option drops the appended NextN block and its associated KV layers, while the mtp option retains only the NextN block along with shared embeddings and the language model head. These technical changes aim to optimize how GLM-5.2 handles token prediction on local hardware across various platforms, including Linux and macOS Apple Silicon.

Khalida Boufedeche has become the first woman ever elected to lead the Algerian Parliament. A medical allergist and member of the National Liberation Front's central committee, she now serves as the fourth highest-ranking official in the state. Her party, the FLN, secured ninety-one seats in the most recent legislative elections, placing them ahead of other groups like the Movement of Society for Peace and the Rally for Culture and Democracy. However, this leadership milestone stands in contrast to a stark lack of female representation within the chamber. Boufedeche leads a body where only twenty-five women hold seats, accounting for just over six percent of the total membership. This political shift follows an election cycle defined by historic apathy, as voter turnout dropped to twenty-one percent, the lowest level ever recorded in the country's history.

The European Central Bank reports that negotiated wage pressures remain stable across its participating countries. According to the latest data, the ECB wage tracker shows smoothed one-off payments of 2.3 percent for 2026. Looking further ahead, that figure rises to 2.7 percent in the first quarter of 2027. This projection is based on a coverage of 28.4 percent of employees. The central bank has extended its forward-looking horizon to March 2027 as more new collective bargaining agreements are signed. Officials expect to extend this window again into the second quarter of 2027 during the September data release. Compared to June figures, these updated numbers show no material change in the assessment of wage pressures for the current year.

China is moving to break the near-monopoly held by the European group ASML over lithography machines. A Chinese company has reportedly begun producing its own DUV, or Deep Ultraviolet, lithography machines to reduce reliance on Western technology. These machines are essential for semiconductor manufacturers like Intel and Samsung to produce chips. The move comes as the Dutch government maintains strict export controls on ASML's most advanced equipment for security reasons. In other news, fact-checkers at Dubawa have flagged a misleading video circulating on Facebook. A page called Arise Again claimed the footage showed bandits attacking a Nigerian military base, but investigators found the video actually depicts an attack by the JNIM insurgent group against security forces in Burkina Faso. The post had gained over 32,000 views before being debunked as recycled conflict footage.

The distinction between merchant shipping and military operations is blurring in the Black Sea as Russia considers arming grain carriers. This move follows claims from Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces that drones struck 201 Russian-linked ships in just over three weeks, including 129 vessels in the Sea of Azov. To protect these shipments, Moscow is discussing fitting bulkers with armor, anti-drone netting, and heavy machine guns, potentially requiring traders to cover the costs of these modifications. While security risks mount in one region, China continues to expand its industrial capacity. COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry is planning a 1.1 billion dollar shipbuilding base in Tianjin featuring two massive drydocks for ships up to 300,000 deadweight tons. Meanwhile, Marine Insight and Infyz Solutions have formed a knowledge partnership to share expertise on AI-driven terminal operations and smart port technologies to help reduce bottlenecks in global supply chains.

Tensions are rising in Manipur’s Noney district after a Central Reserve Police Force CoBRA unit operation near Bitiang village on Wednesday morning. Local sources reported firing near a Naga Volunteer Group training camp, prompting local women to intervene and block security forces from proceeding. In response, the Working Committee of the Joint Tribe Council announced an immediate, indefinite shutdown across areas inhabited by the Zeme, Rongmei, Liangmai, and Inpui communities. Meanwhile, in the United States, state and federal agencies are investigating coordinated cyberattacks that hit operational technology systems at more than 30 community water systems in Minnesota. While drinking water remains safe, cities like Braham briefly took plants offline after attackers shut down operating controls. Contrastingly, in Ghana, the startup Wingxtra is scaling its cargo drone service by joining FasterCapital’s EquityPilot programme. The company builds GPS-navigated drones capable of carrying 10 kilograms for healthcare and urban deliveries.

GOG is working to bring its Galaxy launcher to Linux users. For a decade, the platform has only supported Windows and macOS, where the Galaxy tool allows customers to install and manage their game libraries. While compatible games can already be installed on Linux, the lack of an official launcher forces users to rely on third-party applications like Heroic Games Launcher. Co-CEO Krzysztof Papliński confirmed via email that the company has now hired a specialist to lead this effort. He noted that GOG is actively exploring the best way to implement Linux support and is investing significant time into the project. However, the company is not yet ready to share specific timelines or results for the rollout. This move follows GOG's transition to an independent company at the end of 2025 and a recruitment push that began earlier this year.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be clear with temperatures between 25 and 34 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 10:00, Optikrunde, at 10:30, Research weekly at Gauss, at 11:00, MxM Spotlight, and at 15:00, Gruppenmeeting Gregor and Research Seminar.
Mail worth checking: Amazon notified you that a package was delivered to your neighbor, Schmidt. Also, check Kleinanzeigen for a user inquiry regarding your rattan chairs.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
